idiom_name: entity-per-table mappers with a hand-written join (Diesel / SeaORM)
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance and its ORMs are per-table entity mappers: SeaORM entities each map one table and relate through belongs_to/has_one, with no joined-inheritance construct, and Diesel has the same shape - so the type set is modelled as an enum of variants or as composed structs, and the join across the per-type tables is written out (sql_query / raw_sql!). What replaces the classic mapper is a loader per variant that joins the base and variant tables and reads the kind column into the enum arm. Because there is no class structure to preserve, decide first whether the type set is closed: a closed set is better served by the enum, an open one by composition.
pitfalls: There is no polymorphic load, so dispatch is a match on the enum arm or the kind column; a missing arm silently drops rows rather than failing loudly.
Base and variant data arrive as separate values, so the shared key must be kept in one place - otherwise identity comparisons between two loads of the same object disagree.
